# ClinePass

> Low-cost monthly subscription to access popular open coding models

ClinePass is a — **\$9.99/month** — monthly subscription that gives you reliable access to popular open coding models with **2-5x the API rate limits** of standard access.

It's completely optional. You don't need ClinePass to use Cline, and you can always use any other provider alongside it.

> [card] [Subscribe to ClinePass](https://app.cline.bot/dashboard/subscription?personal=true)
>
> Get started for \$9.99/month and unlock 2-5x the usage on popular open coding models compared to standard API rate.

## How it works

ClinePass is a separate provider in Cline. After subscribing, select **ClinePass** wherever you configure your provider.

* **IDE Extension**: Go to IDE extension settings, set **API Provider** to **ClinePass**, and sign in.

![Cline IDE extension settings with ClinePass selected as the API Provider](https://mintcdn.com/cline-efdc8260/VQWsSIiCvgswf4Wh/assets/clinepass/clinepass-ide-extension.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=VQWsSIiCvgswf4Wh\&q=85\&s=29abe03e6f64acfc069623afa72a7508)

* **CLI**: Go to `/settings` and select **ClinePass** as your provider.

![Cline CLI settings showing ClinePass selected as the provider](https://mintcdn.com/cline-efdc8260/VQWsSIiCvgswf4Wh/assets/clinepass/clinepass-cli.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=VQWsSIiCvgswf4Wh\&q=85\&s=5a990684be35a9429a8251eb7460d950)

## Why ClinePass

Open models have gotten really good. They now reach performance close to proprietary models for coding tasks, and because many providers can serve them competitively, they're usually far cheaper.

However, getting reliable access can be difficult. Providers vary in quality and availability, and standard rate limits can throttle heavy agentic workflows that read files, run commands, and iterate across many turns.

ClinePass solves this by:

* Curating a select group of open models tested and benchmarked for coding agent use
* Offering **2-5x the usage** on popular open coding models compared to standard API rate, so you can run long, complex agent tasks without interruption
* Providing stable access through Cline's infrastructure

content.text:
The five providers are wired up in your order, but none of their parsers is rewritten for the new formats yet, and I haven't run `npm start`. Typecheck, lint and format pass.

**Providers**
1. OpenCode Go, from `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1/models` (JSON)
2. OpenCode Zen, from `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` (JSON)
3. Cursor, from `https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing.md` (markdown). This is a new provider in `src/cursor/`, with a stub parser that throws until a Pi agent writes it.
4. GitHub Copilot, from the `models-and-pricing.yml` URL (YAML)
5. ClinePass, from `https://docs.cline.bot/getting-started/clinepass.md` (markdown)

The order is set in [sources.ts](src/pricing/sources.ts), and I matched it in the workflow's `PROVIDERS` list, the site header and the README.

**What changed in the code**
- `PricingSource` has a new `format` field (html, json, yaml or markdown). The repair agent saves the download as `data/<provider>/source.<ext>` and gets format-specific parsing advice in its prompt.
- I renamed `downloadHtml` to `downloadText`, since the sources are no longer HTML.
- I rewrote each source's row contract (the description of the rows a Pi agent must produce) for its new format. Go's contract maps the JSON fields, including Peak-hour multipliers.
- I installed `yaml` as a direct dependency, as you chose. `package-lock.json` also changed, because `yaml` now resolves to 2.9.1 at the top level.

**Things to know**
- The Zen URL you gave, `/inference/zen/v1/models`, returned 404 on every try. I used `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models`, which returns the full model list and prices.
- Go's JSON gives monthly usage as numbers (`go: 100`, `go-plus: 200`). It isn't clear if that's a dollar cap, so I left that for the Pi agent to handle.
- The existing parsers still target the old HTML. They will throw on the new formats, and that's what dispatches the Pi agents on a run.
- `config/model-mapping.json` will pick up Cursor's models on the next run.
- The daily workflow will fail until the generated parsers are committed.

A run needs your local `.env`, which has `PARSER_REPAIR` set, and it spends Pi model credits on five agents.

content.text:
I added OpenRouter as the sixth and last provider, with a stub parser that throws until a Pi agent writes the real one. Typecheck, lint and format pass, and I haven't run `npm start`.

- **Source:** `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` (JSON). It returned 200 with 469 models. The new files are in `src/openrouter/`, registered at the end of [sources.ts](src/pricing/sources.ts).
- **Row contract:** Prices come as USD per token strings, so the Pi agent must multiply them by 1M. It skips non-text models and auto-router entries with negative prices, and keeps the `modelId` (e.g. `tencent/hy4-flash`).
- **Also updated:** the workflow's `PROVIDERS` list, the site's provider list and description, and the README, which now says six sources.

OpenRouter has hundreds of models, many of them duplicates or variants of models other providers already list. The mapping step will try to match each one to an Artificial Analysis slug, so expect `config/model-mapping.json` to grow a lot on the next run.
